accepted.s: During periods of surplus electricity generation, pumped-storage hydropower primarily performs which operation?
o: Converts thermal energy directly into hydroelectricity
Pumps water from the lower reservoir to the upper reservoir
Stores electricity only in chemical batteries
Releases water from the lower reservoir to the upper reservoir by gravity
accepted.x: In surplus hours, water is pumped from the lower reservoir to the upper reservoir. It is released later during peak demand to generate electricity.
accepted.tq: Test the operating principle by separating charging from discharging.
accepted.sec: Pumped storage - principle, grid role, policy, AP projects

accepted.s: Pumped-storage hydropower is often described as a ‘giant water battery’ because it
o: uses water to absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
stores surplus electricity and releases it during peak demand
stores water permanently without generating electricity
generates electricity only during periods of high rainfall
accepted.x: Pumped-storage systems store surplus electricity by raising water to an upper reservoir and generate power when the stored water is released.
accepted.tq: Apply the storage analogy to the charging and discharging cycle.
accepted.sec: Pumped storage - principle, grid role, policy, AP projects

accepted.s: Which characteristic makes pumped-storage hydropower especially useful for balancing a power grid?
o: It is the fastest-responding large-scale storage option
It functions only when solar generation is absent throughout the year
It is the slowest form of large-scale electricity storage
It eliminates the need for transmission networks
accepted.x: Pumped storage is described as the fastest-responding large-scale storage, making it useful for balancing variable renewable generation and peak demand.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise functional advantage rather than the general description.
accepted.sec: Pumped storage - principle, grid role, policy, AP projects

accepted.s:

accepted.s: Under the classification used by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, small hydropower projects are those with capacity
accepted.x: MNRE classifies hydropower projects up to 25 MW as small hydro, while projects above 25 MW are classified as large hydro by the Ministry of Power.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the administrative history of small hydropower limits?
o: Projects up to 3 MW moved to MNRE in 1989, and the limit became 25 MW in November 1999
Projects up to 25 MW moved to MNRE in 1989, and the limit became 3 MW in 1999
Projects above 25 MW moved to MNRE in 1989

accepted.x: Plants up to 3 MW were moved to MNRE in 1989, and the limit was extended to 25 MW in November 1999.
accepted.tq: Track both the administrative sequence and the associated dates.

accepted.s: Which factor represents a major weakness of hydropower despite its renewable and low-operating-emission characteristics?

accepted.tq: Balance the stated advantages against the specific environmental vulnerability.
